cost: Bounded interval-enumeration oracle work O(sum(n^3*3^n), n=0..8), O(n) temporary space; long fixture O(100000).
forward: Execute 9,841 ternary sequences of lengths 0 through 8 against an independent naive oracle, plus explicit empty/singleton/repetition/UTF-8 and 100,000-byte constant-input fixtures; succeed only when all assertions hold.
Three additional tests check bounded constructive preimages, derived observations and countermodels; six tests total.
inverse: Within the universe of these test runs paired with pass/fail observations, pass is excluded if any specified assertion is false. Fail is excluded when every assertion completes true in the ordinary execution model. Untested inputs and compiler/runtime defects remain outside the observation.

A passing observation admits every candidate implementation agreeing with all checked fixture observations; it cannot identify the source or constrain all untested inputs. A failing observation admits executions with at least one violated assertion; the assertion trace narrows the compatible implementations.
limitations: Partial syntax; finite tests do not prove all inputs; byte rather than Unicode character semantics.
state: Deterministic test executions over the explicitly enumerated finite byte fixtures.
